..
KEY MESSAGE 1...
Temperatures trend several degrees warmer for Friday as we get
into return flow behind the departing high pressure, reaching 
the mid to upper 80s across much of the area. Still carrying
patchy fog across interior portions of the area east of I-71
late tonight into early Friday due to favorable radiational
cooling conditions. Any fog should be confined to the typical 
less urban, lower-lying areas. Dry weather is largely favored to
persist through at least early Saturday across much of the 
area. Do have a slight chance for showers mentioned Friday 
afternoon across portions of interior northern Ohio. Daytime 
heating may yield just enough instability for a few showers to 
try developing as a lake breeze pushes inland. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...
Main focus continues to be an upper trough and associated
surface low that will dive across the western/southern Great
Lakes and northern Ohio Valley this weekend. The surface low is
expected to move east and pull a cold front across the local
area during the day Sunday. Models and ensembles still show 
some spread among the finer details, but are beginning to 
converge on a solution. There has been a modest trend to show a 
more amplified trough, leading to a slightly slower and stronger
surface low that tracks a bit farther northwest. Overall, this 
leads to an increase in the rainfall forecast across the area 
and leads to the chances for rain on Sunday trending higher as 
the cold front crosses the area slower. 

Overall, some showers may graze Northwest Ohio and perhaps Lake
Erie and adjacent lakeshore counties farther east late Friday
night or early Saturday morning as warm air and moisture
advection begins increasing ahead of the approaching system.
Rain potential ramps up from west to east Saturday into Saturday
night...it still looks like eastern OH into PA may be dry for
most of the day Saturday due to a drier easterly low-level flow,
particularly with the system trending a bit slower. Rain
potential is expected to peak late Saturday into early Sunday
when we get into the most favorable region for large-scale lift
just ahead of the approaching shortwave and surface low. With
the system trending a bit slower, the expected drying trend from
the northwest Sunday into Sunday night has trended a bit slower
as well. We should see a gradual drying trend by Sunday night,
though the day Sunday has trended more unsettled/wetter overall. 

The combination of weak mid-level lapse rates (<6.0C/km) and
fairly limited heating will keep a lid on how much instability
can develop this weekend, meaning severe weather potential
should be on the low side. The trend for a more amplified 
system in recent guidance does allow deep-layer shear to 
increase modestly (to around 30kt) Sunday, and the slower trend
may give time for a bit more instability to build ahead of the 
crossing front. So, we'll monitor trends for a lower-end severe
risk across our eastern/southeastern counties Sunday. As 
precipitable water values increase to nearly 2.00" late Saturday
into Sunday amid skinny instability profiles, rainfall rates 
within any convection will become quite efficient. The modest 
trend for a more amplified system does increase potential for 
locally heavy rain across parts of the area, especially between 
late Saturday and early Sunday. We'll need to monitor for any 
locations that see training or repeated convection for localized
heavy rain/flooding concerns. The area has dried out recently, 
so the rain should largely be more beneficial than harmful. 

High temperatures will range from the upper 70s to mid 80s this
weekend (warmer Saturday), with overnight lows and humidity
levels trending up from the last few days. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...
There is some uncertainty regarding how quickly our weekend
system exits. Most models and ensemble members have a quick exit
by Sunday night or early Monday...the GFS cuts off a portion of
the weekend system, with that cut-off low then lingering early
next week across the region. The GFS is viewed as an outlier,
but that overall evolution does contain some uncertainty.
The favored solution is more seasonable temperatures and largely
dry weather for the first half of next week, but the forecast
does contain some lower POPs due to some uncertainty regarding
how quickly the weekend system exits, and due to some
uncertainty regarding how quickly high pressure builds in and
clears out some of the low-level moisture. As ridging builds 
across the western and southern U.S. late next week a more 
unsettled west-northwest flow may try developing across the 
Great Lakes. Overall confidence in any shower/storm chances the 
second half of next week is quite low this far out.
